name: the Mere Neck on the Long road
why_founding: The Long road from Archon to Gideon crosses Middle Argonia on what firm ground it can find. Here that is a strip of ground between two meres, barely higher than the water.
why_site_advantages: The neck is the only dry line between the meres for a long way. For about fifty metres the mere covers the north half of the road, knee-deep and in places to the waist.
why_occupants_motive: The neck has no residents. Travellers drove poles into both verges so that a walker can keep to the causeway when the water covers it.
why_pressures: Poles mark the causeway verge. A walker who strays off the causeway between them goes into deeper water.
why_would_change_if: If the meres dried back, the poles would be left standing on dry ground. No traveller would replace them.
ends_southwest_towards: the marsh track west of the neck

name: the Border road crossings below Greenspring
why_founding: The Border road was laid on a Dunmer line from Stormhold to Thorn. West of the Greenspring track it drops off the ridge into the river marsh.
why_site_advantages: The road keeps to the dry strip at the mountain foot and crosses water only where it must: two reaches of the river marsh, where the water stands up to a metre and a quarter deep.
why_occupants_motive: The crossings have no residents. The people of Greenspring keep the planks in repair because their trade goes out along this road.
why_pressures: The marsh rots the piles in a few seasons. Greenspring has to keep replacing them.
why_would_change_if: A stone causeway would replace the planks if anyone paid for one.
